knowledge:
- key_parameters: threads=controls parallel processing for RNA state preparation in ppRnaInp() and ppRealInp() ;; n_perms=number of permutations to generate/collect for background distribution in ppPermInp() and colPermIPL() ;; sampleids=optional vector of sample IDs to run PARADIGM on in runPrd() and runPermPrd() ;; min_n_gmt_gns=minimum number of GMT genes required when finding the largest pathway subset in subNtw() ;; n_random_runs=number of random clustering runs to evaluate variation due to Louvain clustering randomness in clSamp() ;; min_mtf_n_nodes=minimum number of nodes for a consensus motif in conMtf() ;; min_frc=minimum fraction of samples in a group that must have a GO term significantly over-represented to plot it in pltOvrHm() ;; strat_func=function/threshold (e.g., '>0') to stratify samples based on protein pathway states in pltSttKM()
- alternatives: None mentioned. PARADIGM (Vaske et al.) is the underlying method used to predict pathway levels.
- when_to_use: When you have paired copy-number alteration (CNA) focal-level data and RNA-seq data (both tumor and normal samples) for a cohort of cancer patients, along with a pre-defined biological pathway network, and want to identify patient clusters with distinct pathway profiles and key pathway proteins.
- pitfalls: Requires an external PARADIGM binary (compiled for Linux or macOS) to run runPrd() and runPermPrd(). RNA-seq data requires both tumor and normal samples to evaluate state activation/repression. Louvain clustering in igraph (v1.3+) introduces randomness, so clSamp() should be run multiple times (using n_random_runs) to evaluate clustering variation.

workflows.name: multi_omic_pathway_analysis
workflows.intent: Integrate copy-number alteration and RNA-seq data with pathway networks to identify patient clusters with distinct pathway profiles and key pathway proteins.
input: fake.gmt (Gene set file in GMT format)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare CNA and RNA states from real data using ppRealInp ;; 2. Prepare permuted CNA and RNA states using ppPermInp ;; 3. Run PARADIGM on real and permuted data using runPrd and runPermPrd ;; 4. Collect real and permuted IPLs using colRealIPL and colPermIPL ;; 5. Filter real IPLs by permuted background using fltByPerm ;; 6. Find the largest pathway subset per sample using subNtw ;; 7. Perform gene set over-representation analysis using ovrGMT ;; 8. Cluster samples by over-representation results using clSamp ;; 9. Find consensus pathway motifs within clusters using conMtf ;; 10. Generate diagnostic plots using pltOvrHm, pltConMtf, pltMtfPrtIPL, pltSttKM, and pltNeiStt
workflows.code:
cn_tumor_mat <- system.file('extdata/TcgaInp/focal_tumor.rds',
                            package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
rna_tumor_mat <- system.file('extdata/TcgaInp/log10fpkmP1_tumor.rds',
                            package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
rna_norm_mat  <- system.file('extdata/TcgaInp/log10fpkmP1_normal.rds',
                            package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
real_se <- ppRealInp(cn_tumor_mat, rna_tumor_mat, rna_norm_mat, threads=2)
perml <- ppPermInp(real_se, n_perms=3)
real_se <- system.file('extdata/TcgaInp/inp_real.rds', package='MPAC') |> 
    readRDS()
fpth <- system.file('extdata/Pth/tiny_pth.txt', package='MPAC')
outdir <- tempdir()
paradigm_bin <- '/path/to/PARADIGM'
runPrd(real_se, fpth, outdir, paradigm_bin, sampleids=c('TCGA-CV-7100'))
permll <- system.file('extdata/TcgaInp/inp_perm.rds', package='MPAC') |> 
    readRDS()
pat <- 'TCGA-CV-7100'
runPermPrd(permll, fpth, outdir, paradigm_bin, sampleids=c(pat))
indir <- system.file('/extdata/runPrd/', package='MPAC')
colRealIPL(indir) |> head()
n_perms <- 3
colPermIPL(indir, n_perms) |> head()
realdt <- system.file('extdata/fltByPerm/real.rds', package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
permdt <- system.file('extdata/fltByPerm/perm.rds', package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
fltByPerm(realdt, permdt) |> head()
fltmat <- system.file('extdata/fltByPerm/flt_real.rds', package='MPAC') |>
        readRDS()
fgmt <- system.file('extdata/ovrGMT/fake.gmt', package='MPAC')
subNtw(fltmat, fpth, fgmt, min_n_gmt_gns=1)
subntwl <- system.file('extdata/subNtw/subntwl.rds', package='MPAC') |>readRDS()
omic_gns <- system.file('extdata/TcgaInp/inp_focal.rds', package='MPAC') |>
            readRDS() |> rownames()
ovrGMT(subntwl, fgmt, omic_gns)
ovrmat <- system.file('extdata/clSamp/ovrmat.rds', package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
clSamp(ovrmat, n_random_runs=5)
subntwl <- system.file('extdata/conMtf/subntwl.rds', package='MPAC') |>readRDS()
conMtf(subntwl, omic_gns, min_mtf_n_nodes=50)
ovrmat <- system.file('extdata/pltOvrHm/ovr.rds',package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
cldt   <- system.file('extdata/pltOvrHm/cl.rds', package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
pltOvrHm(ovrmat, cldt, min_frc=0.8)
grphl <- system.file('extdata/pltMtfPrtIPL/grphl.rds',package='MPAC') |>
         readRDS()
proteins <- c('CD28', 'CD86', 'LCP2', 'IL12RB1', 'TYK2', 'CD247', 'FASLG', 
              'CD3G')
pltConMtf(grphl, proteins)
fltmat <- system.file('extdata/pltSttKM/ipl.rds', package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
cldt <- system.file('extdata/pltMtfPrtIPL/cl.rds',package='MPAC')|> readRDS()
pltMtfPrtIPL(fltmat, cldt, grphl, proteins)
cdrmat <- system.file('extdata/pltSttKM/cdr.rds', package='MPAC') |> readRDS()
pltSttKM(cdrmat, fltmat, event='OS', time='OS_days', 
         proteins=c('CD247', 'FASLG'), strat_func='>0')
protein <- 'CD86'
real_se <- system.file('extdata/pltNeiStt/inp_real.rds', package='MPAC') |> 
    readRDS()
fltmat <- system.file('extdata/pltNeiStt/fltmat.rds', package='MPAC') |> 
            readRDS()
pltNeiStt(real_se, fltmat, fpth, protein)
